title: Block B close: prophets and light
hookLine: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Musa, Yusuf, Maryam, Ayyub, Yunus, all in one arc
carry: they all said the same one thing

lines: A SHIP ON DRY LAND, A BOY IN A WELL.
A FIRE, A PALM, A WHALE.
cards: Seventy-two days ago, on day four hundred twenty-nine, Block B opened with Surah Yunus. Since then the path has walked through sixteen surahs, from Yunus to Al-Furqan, crowded with people.
A man building a ship on dry land while his neighbors laughed. Two prophets warning two vanished peoples. A boy thrown into a well who grew up to forgive his brothers.
A man who saw a fire in the desert and walked toward it. A young mother under a palm tree. A sick man who named his pain.
A prophet calling from the dark inside a whale. Different centuries, different places. And yet.

teach.h: NUH, HUD, SALIH; THE FRIENDS OF GOD.
teach.b: Here's Block B in a handful of doors. Yunus and Hud: Nuh and his ark, Hud and Salih sent to 'Ad and Thamud, and the friends of God who neither fear nor grieve. Yusuf: the well, the prison, and no blame on you today.

Ar-Ra'd and Ibrahim: the thunder glorifying, and a good word like a good tree. Al-Isra and Al-Kahf: the night journey, the young men in the cave, and the stranger who explained what Musa couldn't bear.

teach.h: YUSUF; THE CAVE; THE PALM; THE FIRE.
teach.b: Maryam and Ta-Ha: the palm tree in labor, the fire Musa walked toward, and 'ilm, increase me in knowledge.
Al-Anbiya: Ayyub, Zakariyya, and rahmatan lil-'alamin. Al-Hajj, Al-Mu'minun, An-Nur, Al-Furqan: the pilgrims' call, the believers, mishkat, and the servants of the Merciful who walk gently.

Now listen for the line that keeps coming back. Surah Hud tells the stories of Nuh, Hud, Salih and Shu'ayb, and each opens with nearly the same words to his people: worship God; you have no god but Him.

Al-Anbiya says it outright: God sent no messenger before Muhammad ﷺ without revealing to him that there is no god but God, so worship Him. The Qur'an doesn't present these prophets as founders of different faiths.

teach.h: ONE LINE OF MESSENGERS, ONE MESSAGE.
teach.b: It presents them as one long line of messengers, each sent to their own people in their own language, each saying the same one thing. Different storms, different deserts, different kings. One message.
And between the stories, light: on a lamp in a niche, on a pilgrim's road, on a heart that sees.

how: Muslims believe in all the prophets the Qur'an names, from Adam to Muhammad, as one line of messengers bringing the same core message of God's oneness, and add 'peace be upon him' after each name.

o: a holy book sent down to a single people
a founder who starts a new religion
a messenger sent by God to their own people

games.q: Block B's prophets — tap the pairs.
p: built a ship on dry land

s: the Qur'an presents its prophets as founders of different religions
it presents one long line of messengers, each with the same core message.
in Surah Hud, several prophets open with nearly the same words
Nuh, Hud, Salih and Shu'ayb each tell their people: worship God; you have no god but Him.
Block B covered only the stories of prophets
it also held light upon light, the pilgrims' call, and the servants of the Merciful.

games.q: you're a prophet sent to a people who've never heard of you. it's your first sentence to them. what do you say, in the Qur'an's telling?
o: here is a new religion, unlike your fathers'.
worship God; you have no god but Him.
follow me, and I'll make you prosperous.
games.why: in Surah Hud, Nuh, Hud, Salih and Shu'ayb all begin with nearly the same words. they all said the same one thing.

practice: Let the faces of this block pass by slowly: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Yusuf, Musa, Maryam, Zakariyya, Ayyub, Yunus.
Notice which one you stay with, the one in the well, maybe, or the one in the dark, or the one asking not to be left alone, and ask yourself why that one. If you pray, you can send peace on them.

wordCard.voice: Rasul, a messenger: the word for every prophet from Yunus to Al-Furqan, one long line of messengers sent with the same message. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: rasul, a messenger; the Qur'an speaks of messengers sent to every people.

carryVoice: Your line: they all said the same one thing. Tomorrow the path steps into the Islamic year itself, starting with Muharram. See you there.
